The Kwini, also called Yeidji or Gwini, are an Aboriginal people of the north Kimberley in Western Australia, around the coast near present day Kalumburu. They also call themselves Balanggarra, a name now used for the native title group of the area.

The map shows them beside the Yiiji, which is another spelling for much the same people, and near the Gaambera and Miwa. Their language belongs to the Worrorran family. The region is rich in rock art, including the Wandjina figures.

A Benedictine mission, founded on this coast in 1908 and moved to Kalumburu in 1937, drew many Kwini people in during the 1900s. Before that, contact with outsiders was mostly with Makassan trepang fishers, who worked this coast early in their voyages.
